blogs.title: When “Angioedema” Isn’t: Dermatomyositis in the Swollen Neck
blogs.description: A diagnostic deep dive into pseudoangioedema as an unusual presentation of dermatomyositis. This post would focus on how clinicians can distinguish inflammatory cervical oedema from histaminergic or bradykinin-mediated angioedema, using clues such as subacute progression, absent medication/family history, lack of classic airway edema features, and the presence of subtle systemic findings.

blogs.title: The CK That Changed the Case: Using Small Exam Findings to Unmask Inflammatory Myopathy
blogs.description: This post would highlight the bedside pivot points that led away from ENT and angioedema pathways toward dermatomyositis: periungual changes, rash, proximal weakness, dysphagia, and marked creatine kinase elevation. It would emphasize how careful skin and nail examination can uncover an inflammatory myopathy even when classic Gottron’s papules or heliotrope rash are absent.

blogs.title: SAE1 Dermatomyositis: Why This Antibody Matters at the Front Door
blogs.description: A focused review of anti-SAE1 antibody-positive dermatomyositis for acute care and inpatient clinicians. The post would cover its phenotype, including prominent cutaneous disease, frequent dysphagia, possible interstitial lung disease, and malignancy risk, and explain how antibody status can help frame prognosis, organ surveillance, and subspecialty follow-up.

blogs.title: Neck Swelling, Dysphagia, and Aspiration: Airway Thinking Beyond Infection
blogs.description: This post would explore the airway and swallowing implications of inflammatory myopathy involving the head and neck. It would discuss the tension between reassuring oxygenation and clinically important pharyngeal dysfunction, the role of nasendoscopy and swallow studies, recognition of aspiration pneumonitis, and when severe dysphagia should push clinicians toward urgent immunosuppressive treatment.

blogs.title: Treating Severe Dermatomyositis Up Front: Steroids, IVIG, Rituximab, and Steroid-Sparing Strategy
blogs.description: A management-focused post examining why aggressive combination immunosuppression was reasonable in this case of moderate-to-severe dermatomyositis with dysphagia and marked soft tissue inflammation. It would review practical considerations in choosing pulse methylprednisolone, IVIG, mycophenolate, and rituximab, as well as monitoring for treatment complications and selecting Pneumocystis prophylaxis when trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole is not tolerated.

blogs.title: Cancer Screening in Dermatomyositis: How Much Is Enough, and for Whom?
blogs.description: This post would use the case to examine malignancy screening in dermatomyositis, especially in a patient with high-risk features such as dermatomyositis itself, dysphagia, male sex, and anti-SAE1 positivity. It would discuss how current risk-stratified guidance informs baseline CT/PET imaging, endoscopic evaluation, interval surveillance, and the limits of tumor markers in real-world practice.
